so too does a cultural world view, We

Yet, despite the struggles facing
initiatives such as WOLP, there are
historical examples that point to the
possibility that language restoration is
no mere academic pipe dream, The
revival of a form of Hebrew in the 19th
century is often cited as one of the best
proofs that languages long d

urrected and embraced
In the meantime, the race is on to
coliect and protect as many of the
languages as possible, so that future
generations can continue their
itions and have a sense of identity.
And it certainly is a race: Turin knows
his project's limits and believes it
inevitable that a large number of those
languages will die out. ‘We have to be
wholly realistic. A project like ours is in
no position to, and was not designed to
keep languages alive. The only people
who can help languages survive are the
people in those small communities
themselves. They need to be reminded
that it’s good to speak theirown
language. Becoming modern doesn’t
mean you have to stop using your _
language. I think it’s important they
understand that.’
